propositions: Marker tokens (VOTER_ERROR, MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR, RECONCILE_DEGRADED, ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR, LLM_TOKEN_USAGE) are emitted twice to journald when logging is configured: once via logger call and once via stderr print

The configure_logging() StreamHandler attaches a stdout sink with %(message)s format that captures and re-emits the line-start marker prefix, causing the observability.sh anchored grep to count each real error twice

The observability probe's anchored count (grep -cE '^TOKEN {') matches both the logger-stream copy and stderr print, violating the single-emission contract that one real error must produce one countable line

Four emitter sites pass the token-prefixed marker string to both logger calls and stderr prints: voter.py _voter_error and _emit_token_usage, voter_merge.py merge_change_error, reconcile.py _degraded, artifact_emit.py _artifact_emit_error

The fix retains the unconditional stderr print as the sole line-start emission and changes logger calls to emit only the structured record body without the token prefix, keeping the log-stream visible but unmatchable by the probe anchor
A structural class-guard test prevents future markers from reintroducing the dual line-start emission construct
